title: Scott Aaronson (Nov 27): he has "specific information" that AI labs will soon release a major theoretical-cryptanalysis breakthrough that will not endanger currently deployed cryptosystems, and still has no actionable information on rumors of more serious breaks
quote_verbatim: will not lead to imminent danger for any currently deployed cryptosystems
what_is_new: Follow-up to the Nov 25 "virtually certain" bombshell post (Run 44 item 013) and the Bank of England comments (Run 45 item 001). In a satirical Thanksgiving-call post he now splits two claims: (1) specific information, which he says he cannot give on the record, of a coming theoretical-cryptanalysis result that will not endanger deployed systems; (2) "endless rumors" of more serious breaks, which he takes seriously on priors but for which he has "no specific, actionable information." No lab has confirmed either claim. A Guardian piece dated Nov 28 repeats the broader rumor and was not fully opened (403).
why_for_agiright: The main public source on the crypto-break rumor now draws a line between a coming theoretical result and unverified claims of a practical break, and still no lab has confirmed anything.
doubts: Blog post read in full, including the update on how the post was headlined on X. Guardian 403; Quantum State news write-up also opened as a check. Reports stay reports until a lab or paper appears.

title: Bloomberg (via Engadget and Techmeme): Chinese filings show restricted NVIDIA Blackwell hardware (a GB300 NVL72 rack and GB200 servers) at the Yangtze River Delta Project in Shanghai, a data center linked to Alice Huang and Megaspeed; Bloomberg says it has no evidence Megaspeed directly diverted the chips
author_or_publisher: Engadget, reporting Bloomberg; seen via Techmeme
quote_verbatim: Bloomberg notes it does not have evidence that Megaspeed directly diverted NVIDIA chips
what_is_new: Owner rule 2026-11-12: Jensen Huang / NVIDIA succession logged as governance, not gossip. Official wording: Board "reinstated" him (newsroom and 8-K, Nov 23); other words belong to their source; conflicting reports side by side, unreconciled; reports stay reports until a primary document exists. Bloomberg, citing serial numbers in Chinese regulatory filings: Shanghai Shuoyao listed a GB300 NVL72 rack as collateral for a loan; the serial traces to Taiwan's Gigabyte, which would not say who first bought it. Shuoyao has called itself a Megaspeed service provider. Megaspeed used renderings of the project in a 2024 investor deck without naming China. Bloomberg also reports Hopper-generation chips at the site and lists Kang Wei as the facility's president. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing; the Justice Department is already investigating whether it broke US export rules. Bloomberg.com 403; Engadget opened in full.
why_for_agiright: New reported physical evidence that export-controlled Blackwell systems are in a Shanghai facility tied to the Megaspeed/Alice Huang diversion story, days before the Dec 1-3 congressional sessions.
doubts: Secondary report of Bloomberg; the Bloomberg article itself 403 and Bloomberg Law page was a shell. NVIDIA had no comment to Engadget. Reports stay reports; no new 8-K or newsroom release.

title: UK House of Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee (chair Liam Byrne) publishes a 27 November letter asking Anthropic for the full unredacted METR report on AI R&D acceleration, or the omitted material and an explanation of the redactions; reply requested by 4 December
author_or_publisher: UK House of Commons Business, Innovation, Science and Trade Committee (Rt Hon Liam Byrne MP); official catalogue plus Snape Report
quote_verbatim: Letter to Anthropic relating to the report from Model Evaluation & Threat Research (METR) on AI research and development at Anthropic
what_is_new: The official committee catalogue lists the letter (publication 56062, file "Letter - 27.11.2026 - BTC Chair to Anthropic on METR's R&D report.pdf"), published 27 November 2026 at 12:15 UK time, under the "AI adoption, safety and governance" work package. The PDF itself was blocked (Cloudflare 403). Per Snape Report, it is addressed to Pip White, Anthropic UK and Ireland, and asks for the full report or the omitted material and an explanation of the redactions, with a reply by Friday 4 December. METR's 5 November public assessment (already on the site) said Anthropic is likely improving capabilities at about twice its earlier rate, largely by using its own AI, but that Anthropic redacted most of the evidence METR found most informative. Seen in the Following feed via @discoplomacy, reposted by @ShakeelHashim and quoted by @AndrewCurran_.
why_for_agiright: A parliamentary committee is now formally asking a frontier lab to unredact an independent assessment of how fast the lab is using AI to speed its own research.
doubts: Official catalogue page opened and read; the letter PDF was Cloudflare-blocked, so the addressee, the 4 December deadline and the request to explain redactions are from Snape Report (opened), not from the PDF itself.

title: LithoWar (via Techmeme): the US MATCH Act could backfire by barring ASML from servicing its roughly 350 immersion scanners in China, letting rivals service and reverse-engineer them and hire its staff
quote_verbatim: How the MATCH Act could backfire by barring ASML from its ~350 immersion scanners in China
